questions: Is slalom line_loss_events 0 at y=0.067 m with the ±0.065 m spread? If not, report the max_error at the first loss.
Does s-bend progress stay at or above about 0.15, or does it fall toward 0.04 as in iteration 7?
Does slalom max_error fall below 0.06 m? Report it per track.
Does slalom steering_oscillation fall below 0.10? If not, lead and speed are not its cause.
Does the oval still stop at progress 0.115 with max_error about 0.061 m? If so, the oval failure is a fixed track feature.
feedback_request.requested_changes_if_any: If line loss stays at 1 per run on slalom at y=0.067 m with zero s-bend loss, keep the ±0.065 m spread and the 0.03 m speed, and do not move the row further. If slalom max_error is still at or above 0.06 m with zero line loss, widen the spread to ±0.08 m with 16 mm footprints. If the score is at or above 56.4 with zero line loss, keep the geometry fixed and test sensor_size 0.012 m at the same positions.

intent: Keep iteration 8's ±0.065 m, 16 mm sensor layout and move only the forward row from y=0.07 m to y=0.067 m. Aim: remove the remaining slalom line loss (1 per run in iteration 8) while keeping most of the s-bend progress gain (0.1825). Expected score 53 to 58, with slalom line_loss_events near 0 and slalom max_error below 0.06 m. If line loss stays at 1 on slalom, the lead is not the trigger at this speed and the next lever is the controller, not geometry.
learning: Iteration 8 showed that the ±0.065 m spread cut s-bend line loss (1 to 0.05 per run) and raised s-bend progress, while the y=0.07 m lead still lost the line on slalom. The next race tests whether a 3 mm lead reduction removes that slalom loss without giving back the s-bend gain.
rationale: Iteration 8 is the best design so far (56.40). Relative to iteration 3 (51.31, spread ±0.05 m at y=0.07 m), widening the spread to ±0.065 m cut s-bend line loss from 1 per run to 0.05 per run and lifted s-bend progress to 0.1825. Slalom still loses the line once per run, with max_error 0.0604 m (just above the 0.06 m limit) and steering_oscillation 0.131. The Integrator's rule applies directly: line loss returned at y=0.07 m with the ±0.065 m spread, so the spread is kept and the row is moved to y=0.067 m. This tests whether a slightly smaller lead cuts slalom line loss while keeping most of the s-bend gain. Iteration 7 (y=0.065 m) showed that going too far forward-back costs s-bend progress (it fell to 0.04), so 0.067 m is a small step, not a fall-back. Speed stays at wheel_radius 0.03 m, since 0.04 m caused line loss in iteration 6. The oval stays fixed at progress 0.115 across all iterations, so I do not expect a change there. Body, mass, wheel track, footprint size and gains are unchanged from iteration 8, so the race isolates the row position.
